summary:
I've written plan.md: a long, low single-storey house of white stucco and dark timber under a pale slab roof that rises only 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span. Its eaves are 2 deep, beam ends stick out past them every 3 cells, and a flat carport roof sits one level lower beside it. The street side is blank apart from a tan ledgestone wall, a clerestory strip and an orange door; the back is floor-to-ceiling glass between dark posts, opening onto a kidney pool. Those layered horizontals, the central atrium and the teal-and-white car on the driveway are what make it read as an Eichler or Palm Springs house. Long white-stucco, dark-timber post-and-beam bungalow: stepped-slab near-flat gable on beam lines every 3, flat carport deck one level lower, blank street face with ledgestone wall and orange door, all-glass garden side, open-sky atrium at the centre.
Open-plan public core (gallery, galley kitchen, dining, living with sunken pit and freestanding fireplace) west of the atrium; corridor with 3 bedrooms and 2 baths east.
Teal/white car, desert front yard, kidney pool and patio behind. 6 parts; elements.md and the plan.md designer sections are written.

house shell and ground: Part 1 shell done in parts/shell.mjs: bedding, floor slab with room finishes (terrazzo/spruce/quartz), perimeter walls with plan OPENINGS left as air, dark_oak header skipping beam lines, atrium ring base and header, interior partitions and doorways, y=5 spruce ceiling. make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt: 1860 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
polish: Part 1 leaves the corner posts (x=10/31, z=8/25, y=2..4), the whole south glass wall body (y=2..4), the atrium ring body and the clerestory y=4 cells as AIR for part 4 to fill (intended, noted in plan.md Notes).
The y=5 ceiling and south/ring header bays float in `mcd check` (30 floating blocks) until part 3 beams and part 4 glass/posts support them; expected at this stage.
Checked the render at the front-left and back-elevation tiles only; the interior openings and doorways were built from the plan tables but not inspected cell by cell in the render.
Element ticks 1, 7, 13, 16 are set in elements.md, but 13 and 16 are only partly mine: the gap cells and the ring/posts' glazing belong to part 4.

waste.what: Worked out the OPENINGS and partition/doorway cell lists by hand from plan.md's tables (corner posts, south glass wall, clerestory y=4, entry recess, window and door cells, doorways at x=25 z=10/15/19, x=22 z=19..20).
waste.cost: About 25 min of reasoning across the rules, roughly 40 conditional cell rules in code; no retries on the geometry itself.
waste.tool: A helper that reads plan.md's OPENINGS and PARTITIONS tables and turns them into air/white cell lists (or an openings-to-cells parser in vocab.mjs) would have removed the hand transcription.

waste.what: Mapped each floor cell to its ROOMS box and floor kind by hand (bedroom spruce, bath quartz, public terrazzo), with a fallback for the x=25 partition column and the gallery edges.
waste.cost: One loop with a room lookup; written once, no retries.
waste.tool: A rooms.json-to-floor helper (floor kind per room name, respecting pit/atrium/chimney exclusions) in vocab.mjs would have made this one call.

waste.what: Wrote my own terrazzo fleck function because vocab's terrazzo_floor and rng are not exported and take a box, not a cell list.
waste.cost: Small; one helper.
waste.tool: Export rng and a cell-list form of terrazzo_floor from vocab.mjs.

waste.what: Ran the mcd CLI with an MCD shell variable in zsh; the variable did not word-split and the command failed, then I used the direct path. Also BSD sed -i needed an empty suffix argument, which cost a failed sed run.
waste.cost: Two failed commands, about a minute.
waste.tool: Put the mcd invocation in a PATH-visible wrapper (or note in the brief that MCD must be a function or direct path in zsh); a check flag that marks ceilings and bays floating only until the roof stage would have cut the expected FLOATING noise.

summary: site, carport and paving: parts/site.mjs builds the ground cover (sand yard, gravel beds, sidewalk, driveway with joints, stepping pads, landing), the carport (posts, beams, smooth_stone_slab deck, fascia, floor), the breeze screen at z=21, the patio and pool deck, and the lawns, with the kidney pool cells left open. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: site 933 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows no floating or unsupported blocks from this part (the two white_concrete screen cells beside the z=20 post are flagged as orphans, which is the intended screen).
polish: Part 5 (front) saguaro() sand under the cactus cells will be refused by runParts because these cells are gravel from this part; the plan calls the cactus bed gravel, so this is intended but worth a glance when part 5 is merged.
Item 21 (desert planting) and item 24 (patio and pool deck) are only partly built here: sand, gravel and paving are mine, while palms, cacti, mailbox, loungers and the pool are parts 5 and 6.
plan.md PARTS 2 says x=9 z=8..25 is sand; I made it sand only at z=22..25, because the carport floor takes x=9 z=7..21 (recorded in plan.md Notes).

waste.what: Worked out the rectangle and skip-pool coordinates for each ground-cover layer by hand (sand, gravel, paving, patio, deck, lawn) and wrote the lawn claim-logic as a loop with per-cell exclusions.
waste.cost: About 60 coordinate decisions and one rewrite of the lawn loop; roughly 4 minutes of the 12.
waste.tool: A `rect(g, x0,x1,z0,z1,y,block,{skip:pool})` helper in vocab.mjs (with a claimed-cells set), so a part states rectangles and the pool/patio exclusions instead of hand-looping.

waste.what: Resolved a conflict in plan.md between the x=9 sand strip (z=8..25) and the carport floor (x=1..9, z=7..21) and the lawn extent (x=0..9, z=22..33) by reading FLOORS against PARTS; noted it in plan.md Notes.
waste.cost: Reasoning only, no retries, but it is a spec ambiguity other parts may hit.
waste.tool: Plan detail: a single ground-cover table (x, z, y=0, block, owner part) with the overlaps listed, so the carport floor, strips and lawns are one source of truth.

waste.what: Ran mcd with $MCD set to 'node <path>' in zsh; the variable did not word-split and the command failed.
waste.cost: One failed call and one retry.
waste.tool: Use a direct path or `node $M` with M set to the script path only; make.sh's MCD variable has the same zsh issue if it is ever used in a pipeline.

summary:
roofs, beams and fireplace stack: parts/roofs.mjs builds the stepped slab roof (4 bands + fascia ring with atrium and chimney holes), beam_line on x=10..31 at y=5, y=6 gable-end and atrium-ring glass, and the fireplace stack via vocab fireplace_stack. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with 738 roof-part blocks, no refused writes, all ids on the palette.
Front-left and front elevation renders show a low two-tier slab roof with dark fascia, beam tails, the atrium hole and the black flue on the roof.
Checked, not rebuilt: plan.md checklist, elements.md items 2, 3 and 14 ticked; plan.md Notes line added for the local glass loops.
polish: Roof band/fascia uses roof_band and fascia_ring as written in vocab; I did not inspect the gable-end ridge profile closely at close range, only the two overview renders.
Element 27 (fireplace stack) is built here but its tick belongs to the living room part; the room designer should tick it.
check reports 16 orphan beam-end logs at z=5 and z=28 (x=10..19 and so on); these are the intended exposed beam tails past the eave, not a defect.

waste.what: Wrote the eight roof_band calls, the two fascia/band row ranges and the y=6 glass loops by hand, working each z range out from the ROOF_BANDS table
waste.cost: about 3 minutes and one full file rewrite; the table in vocab.mjs was already there
waste.tool: A vocab helper roof_all(g) that loops ROOF_BANDS and calls roof_band per entry, plus a glass_cells(g, [x,y,z0],[x,y,z1]) helper for the gable and ring glass

waste.what: Ticked plan.md and elements.md by hand, reading each file for the exact line text before the Edit
waste.cost: one Read per file plus four Edits
waste.tool: A checklist tool: mcd tick <file> <item> that flips the box and reports the element's part

waste.what: Checked palette membership and refused/off-palette by grepping palette.json and reading the make.sh output
waste.cost: two greps; the part-level REFUSED/OFF-PALETTE line is not printed by make.sh
waste.tool: make.sh (or build.mjs) should print a per-part OFF-PALETTE count, not only placed/refused

waste.what: Ran $MCD as a shell variable in zsh; it failed because the variable was not word-split
waste.cost: one failed command, then a retry with the path set directly
waste.tool: Put a mcd wrapper script on PATH, or document that make.sh should export a MCD function for the parts

summary: facades, glazing and entry: ["parts/facades.mjs builds the south glass wall (dark_oak_log posts on every beam line, glass_pane between, slider gaps glazed at y=4 only), the atrium ring glass, corner posts, the west/east windows and the open dark_oak_door utility door at (10,2..3,10).", "North: the clerestory strip at z=8 y=4 with mullions, the ledgestone feature wall at z=7 x=11..17 with its y=5 cap, and orange_entry at x=18..20 z=8..9. The gable-end y=6 glass is set air-only, so part 3 may duplicate it harmlessly.", "make.sh produced a whole build.nbt: facades placed 218, refused 0, offPalette none. Checklist and elements 4, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14 and 15 are ticked; 13 and 16 were already ticked by part 1."]
polish: The gable-end glass at x=10/31, y=6 (elements 14) is also set by part 3; my glass_bay is air-only, so whichever part runs first wins and the other is a no-op. check.mjs flags it as floating until the roof exists.
The ring glass at y=6 where it crosses band C (x=16/22, z=14..17) is part 3's job and is not built here.
The check reports floating glass and spruce at y=5-6 until the roof part lands. The south wall and ring are supported by part 3's beam lines, which are not in this build yet.
The elevation and tile renders were checked by eye at low resolution only; a closer look at the south glass wall should happen once the roofs part is in.

waste.what: Wrote custom per-cell loops for the south wall and the ring because glass_bay fills every air cell, which would glaze the slider gaps (y=2..3) and the atrium door cells (x=19..20, y=2..3); worked out the exclusions by hand.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of coordinate logic and 2 rewrites of the ring code
waste.tool: a glazing helper such as glazed_wall(g, axis, fixed, a0, a1, {y0,y1, skip:[[x,y,...]], posts:[...]}) or a glass_bay option that skips the slider and door cells, so the parts stop re-deriving the openings

waste.what: Hand-built the two-half dark_oak_door state (open=true, facing west, dropping the powered key that the vocab filters out) because there is no vocab door helper.
waste.cost: one helper written inline, one retry on the state keys
waste.tool: a door_pair(g, x, z, facing, material, open) helper in vocab.mjs that writes both halves with the toolkit-listed states

waste.what: Checked the facade by eye on 300px tiles; the elevation view is too small to confirm the posts and slider glass at y=4.
waste.cost: 3 renders read at low resolution, no zoomed check
waste.tool: mcd render with a zoom or crop option and a layer/slice print of one wall plane (e.g. z=25) as text via layers()

waste.what: A zsh shell variable MCD='node path' was not word-split, so the first mcd call failed.
waste.cost: one failed call and a re-run
waste.tool: put the toolkit on PATH or add a wrapper script for mcd in the crew directory

summary:
car and front garden: parts/front.mjs builds the car_50s on the driveway, palms at (12,3) and (30,4) with persistent crowns, the cactus cluster (saguaro (26,3,h3), (24,2,h2), barrel cacti (28,2), (23,4), (29,4)), a dead_bush at (25,6) and the mailbox at (9,1).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the front line is 108 placed with no REFUSED writes and no OFF-PALETTE blocks. The render shows the car, palms and cacti where the plan puts them.
Checklist ticked in plan.md (5 front) and elements.md items 20, 21, 22; a Notes line records the sand/gravel conflict.
polish: Palm crowns: check reports 8 ORPHAN jungle_leaves at y=6 (the radius-2 cells in the plan's crown spec, e.g. 14,6,3 and 30,6,6). These come from the spec'd crown shape, not a bug, and they leave no structural error; they could be trimmed if the checker must be clean.

Cactus base: the sand-under-each-cactus from element 21 applies only where site leaves plain dirt at y=0. If site paves those cells with gravel, the cacti stand on gravel. The site part should decide and plan.md Notes records it.
Dead bush position (25,6) is my choice; plan.md names only that it sits on the sand.

waste.what: Worked out the cactus and palm coordinates and the dead-bush spot by hand from plan.md's prose, with no tool that lists the placements for the front yard.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate choices plus a re-read of plan.md lines 25-40, 141-160 and 220-260
waste.tool: A plan-to-code stub generator, or a plan.md table the parts can read as data (x, y, z, helper, args).

waste.what: vocab.mjs saguaro() and barrel_cactus() write SAND at y=0 unconditionally, which collides with the earlier site part's gravel bed under runParts ownership; I wrapped the grid in a proxy that only writes that sand onto plain dirt.
waste.cost: one proxy wrapper (about 12 lines) plus one failed-plan reasoning pass
waste.tool: A vocab option such as cactus helpers taking a ground argument, or a shared rule that base cells are written only where air or dirt.

waste.what: vocab.mjs palm() places jungle_leaves without persistent=true, which plan and elements require; I re-set every crown leaf in a second loop.
waste.cost: one helper loop (about 8 lines) and a rebuild
waste.tool: palm(g, x, z, { persistent: true }) option in vocab.mjs.

waste.what: Ran the toolkit through a shell variable (MCD="node ...") that zsh does not word-split, so the first check and render calls failed and needed a retry with the path stored in a variable.
waste.cost: one retry
waste.tool: An mcd wrapper script on PATH (for example bin/mcd) so each part does not have to build the node invocation.

summary:
pool, patio and garden details: parts/back.mjs builds the kidney pool (water and quartz coping; liner and floor fall below y=0), three loungers and a patio table on the patio, a palm at (29,31), four garden lamps (two on the entry path, two by the pool), and a hash-picked short_grass scatter on lawn cells. make.sh runs whole: 169 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
The render shows pool, loungers, palm and lamps where plan.md puts them.
short_grass is conditional on grass_block lawn cells, so it is not yet placed; it appears when site.mjs lays the lawn.
polish: No parasol on the patio table: step 6 asks for one, but plan.md's VOCABULARY note says no parasol. Noted in plan.md Notes; decide whether to add one.
short_grass not yet placed: it needs grass_block lawn cells from site.mjs (part 2), which are still stubs in this copy. It should appear at merge time.
Entry lanterns mentioned in step 6 are not built here; they belong to the facades part (orange_entry).
check reports orphan jungle_leaves on the palm crown (x 27..31, z 29..33, y 6): this is the palm() helper's own crown, so it is cosmetic and left as is.

waste.what: Worked out the lamp, lounger and patio-table coordinates by hand against the patio, deck and lawn extents in plan.md
waste.cost: about 4 coordinate checks, one lamp-cell air check that failed silently on the first try
waste.tool: a plan-coordinate query (e.g. mcd plan cells <kind>) that returns the free cells of a named zone

waste.what: Re-derived the render-view flags by reading the toolkit source; no short render option gives a back oblique view
waste.cost: two extra render calls and a grep through render/views.mjs
waste.tool: mcd render --view back-oblique (or a documented list of --closeups views)

waste.what: Checked whether each cell was air before every write, one call at a time
waste.cost: around 20 isAir guards, written by hand
waste.tool: a vocab helper that writes only into air and reports skipped cells

summary:
room: gallery: Room gallery (parts/room-1.mjs) is built: an orange_carpet entry mat at (19,2,10) and three hung lanterns at y=4 over x=17, 19, 21, inside the one-cell-deep box x=16..22, z=10.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt with 4 gallery blocks placed, no refused or off-palette writes. Walk check: 7/7 standable and reached. Light: floor min 12, so no dark cells.
The bench and coat-hook wall are not built: the box is a one-cell-deep walkway, and any slab or furniture on the floor cut the route to the kitchen opening. Plan note added to plan.md.
polish: Gallery bench (elements.md item 30) not built: the one-cell-deep box leaves no floor cell off the walkway.
Coat-hook wall and item-frame art (item frames are entities, not blocks) not built.
Lantern at (19,4,10) reads UNSUPPORTED in `mcd check` until roofs.mjs lays beam_line x=19 at y=5; the other two lanterns sit under the shell's spruce ceiling.
Lit item (elements.md 35) is only partly met: the gallery's lanterns are in, but the checklist item stays unticked.

waste.what: Checked the gallery layout by hand: parsing the plan grid and deciding which floor cells must stay clear of the kitchen, corridor and atrium openings.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls of reasoning over the plan grid; the plan command printed the grid but I still had to work out the walkway cells by reading it
waste.tool: A `plan --rooms` variant that marks the required walkway cells (ways in to ways out) so a designer knows the free cells without reading the grid.

waste.what: Tried several bench and furniture layouts by trial and error: built, ran make, walked, and removed the bottom slabs that blocked the route.
waste.cost: 2 make+walk cycles
waste.tool: A walk-aware placement check (`mcd walk --dry` on a candidate list of blocks before writing them) so an unwalkable layout is caught before building.

waste.what: Used zsh with an unquoted MCD variable holding 'node path', which failed to expand; I had to call node with the full path each time.
waste.cost: 1 failed command
waste.tool: A quoted or single-word mcd binary in the make.sh/brief so that `$MCD` works in zsh.

summary:
room: kitchen: Kitchen (room-2) built in parts/room-2.mjs: galley on the north wall (quartz counters, cauldron sink, smoker hob, iron-block fridge, orange backsplash, spruce upper cabinets), a second counter run with barrel and potted cactus on z=11, and a spruce-fence breakfast bar on z=13 with birch stair stools on z=12.
Lighting: two hanging lanterns plus a standing lantern. The kitchen floor reads min 10, mean 12, no dark cells. Walkability is ok (16/16 reached). make.sh ran and placed 31 kitchen blocks with no refusals.
Left the vocab galley_kitchen helper unused: its counter on z=10 would block the utility-door route at (11,10).
polish: Hung lantern at (13,4,13) hangs from the beam line x=13 at y=5, which is the roofs part's job; in this stub copy it reads unsupported, and the merged build should be fine.
Fridge trapdoors skipped (they would block the gallery-to-aisle route at (15,10)); the fridge is a plain 2-high iron block.
The bar is spruce fence legs under a bottom spruce slab at y=3 (surface about 3.5), not the plan's top-slab-on-fence; stools are birch_stairs, not the bar_stool vocab helper.
plan.md's checklist lists only the six exterior parts, so room 29 is ticked in elements.md only. Exterior tiles were rendered but the kitchen is interior-only, so I did not inspect them.

waste.what: Placed all 31 kitchen blocks one cell at a time with g.set calls, working out each x/z coordinate by hand from the plan grid.
waste.cost: about 31 explicit set calls and a rewrite after the first layout; roughly 4 minutes of the 12.
waste.tool: layers(g, origin, legend, rows) with the `mcd plan` floor grid pasted as the draft would have placed the whole room in one call; the same grid is what I used by hand.

waste.what: Shell `mcd` calls via a $MCD variable failed twice under zsh (no word-splitting), and the toolkit path had to be retyped in full each time.
waste.cost: 2 failed calls and one 120s background timeout while searching for mcd.mjs.
waste.tool: A `mcd` wrapper script on PATH, or a MCD path in the job prompt that the shell can use directly.

waste.what: The vocab galley_kitchen helper puts its counter on z=10, which blocks the utility-door route at (11,10); I had to read it and write my own layout instead of reusing it.
waste.cost: one read of vocab.mjs and a redesign of the layout.
waste.tool: plan.md note or vocab doc saying galley_kitchen keeps the z=10 aisle free, or a walk check run on a helper's output before use.

summary:
room: dining: parts/room-3.mjs builds the dining room in its box x11..15 z14..18 (y2..4): spruce-fence table with spruce slab top, three birch-stair chairs each side, sideboard under the west window with spruce panelling, pendant lantern on the x=13 beam.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the dining line reads 26 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
Walk check: 23/23 standable cells reached, verdict ok. Light: min 8, mean 11.2, no dark cells. Rendered from above and inside, and the table and chairs read.
polish: The pendant lantern at 13,4,15 reports UNSUPPORTED in mcd check until parts/roofs.mjs lays the dark_oak_log beam at x=13, y=5 (the roof part is still a stub in this copy).
Chairs are birch_stairs and the table top is a spruce_slab, so the room reads as a table and six chairs. Wall and floor parts are other workers' work and are not checked here.
plan.md's checklist has no room rows, so I did not tick anything there. elements.md item 28 is ticked. Item 35 (lit) is not ticked: this room has one lantern and needs the beam to support it.
The 'terrazzo floor' is the shell's, not part of this module; I did not place floor blocks.

waste.what: Worked out the table, chair and sideboard cell coordinates by hand, and tried a dining_set helper that put its lantern over an unsupported cell.
waste.cost: about 3 edit cycles
waste.tool: A vocab helper for a 3x2 table with stair chairs on the long sides, placed from the room box and a clearance rule (the lane must stay open), plus a hang-point check so lanterns only go under beams.

waste.what: Ran the mcd CLI with a $MCD variable holding 'node <path>' in zsh, which does not word-split, so the first calls failed.
waste.cost: 2 failed commands
waste.tool: Note in the crew brief: call the mcd path directly (or use a shell function), since $MCD does not word-split in zsh.

summary:
room: living: parts/room-4.mjs builds the living room: sunken pit with coffee table and orange cushions, orange sofa on the west, egg chair facing the atrium glass, sideboard and floor lamp on the south side, spruce panelling on the x=21 inside wall, and four hung lanterns (min light 8, no dark cells).
make.sh runs clean for this part (57 placed, no refusals, no off-palette), walk check ok (50 of 51 standable cells reached), and the room render reads as a pit-and-sofa show room.
Elements item 27 ticked; item 34 (period furniture) is only partly done. The fireplace is part 3's and was left alone.
polish: Second orange sofa and the tulip side table are not built: the cells that would fit a second sofa block the walkway from the atrium doors to the pit, and a side table has no free cell that keeps a path.
Fireplace stack (x=20..21 z=21..22) is part 3's (parts/roofs.mjs); the living room leaves those cells clear and does not build them. Until part 3 lands, the fireplace cells are empty.
Shell/header floating blocks in the check output (17,5,18), (20,5,18) and (20..21,5,20) are not from this part; the roof part should support them.
Terrazzo floor is not laid by this part: the shell already places the public floor at y=1 and the locked-write rule keeps this part out of it.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture layout by hand against the room box, the doorway/slider walkways and the fireplace cells, then tested it by running the build and walk check, rather than laying it out in the room's plan grid first.
waste.cost: about 3 build-check cycles; one walkway conflict (second sofa) dropped after reasoning about routes by hand
waste.tool: `$MCD plan` drawn with a furniture-candidate pass plus a walk preview that rejects a layout before writing it would have shown the walkway conflicts up front

waste.what: conversation_pit always fills the y=0 pit floor, which the shell already placed, so every call produced 20 REFUSED writes; I wrapped g in a Proxy to skip y=0.
waste.cost: one failed build run plus a proxy hack
waste.tool: vocab.mjs conversation_pit should take a floor=false flag (or skip identical blocks instead of refusing them)

waste.what: sideboard() hard-codes its trapdoor front to south for axis x and east for axis z, so a sideboard against a wall can't face into the room without hand-writing the cells.
waste.cost: one helper call judged wrong on sight, not rewritten
waste.tool: vocab sideboard should take a front= argument

waste.what: Hung-lantern placement: I guessed which cells have a ceiling above (13,4,24 had none) and only found out from the structure check.
waste.cost: one rebuild cycle
waste.tool: `$MCD check` could list which candidate cells have a block above before placing, or the helper could assert support

waste.what: Read the render and fixed by eye; no way to tell the egg chair apart from a sofa stair at this scale.
waste.cost: one look, no fix
waste.tool: a labelled-furniture view in `$MCD rooms` (name each helper's footprint) would make the render check quicker

summary:
room: atrium: Atrium (room-5) built in parts/room-5.mjs: jungle sapling focal with a standing lantern, large ferns and potted cacti in the planting, 2-wide smooth_stone_slab path between the doors, birch_stairs bench on the east, spruce fence + slab side table SW.
make.sh exits 0 with a whole build.nbt; atrium placed 48, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks. Walk: all rooms ok; light: atrium min 8, mean 10.8, 2 lanterns.
Checked the room render (from above and inside) and the house tile; the atrium reads as a planted courtyard. Ticked elements.md item 17 and added an atrium note to plan.md.
polish: The grass patch is short_grass tufts, not a grass_block patch: the shell locks y=0 as dirt under the atrium.
The 'small jungle sapling' is a 4-high jungle tree (trunk 2, crown to y=4), which is the tallest the room box allows.
The check reports floating y=5 header/ceiling blocks in the house (x=14..21, z=18..25); those belong to parts 1 and 3, not this room.
Rocks and a 'tree-fern' theme from elements item 17 are not built; the palette has no rock block, so the item reads as jungle planting plus ferns.

waste.what: Worked out the 5x6 atrium layout cell by cell (planting, path, bench, table, tree crown) and checked the light map by hand against lantern positions
waste.cost: about 2 light-check iterations and one lantern moved after min light came out at 7
waste.tool: a `mcd light --suggest` option that proposes lantern cells to reach a min light level, or a `mcd plan` that prints the light map beside the grid

waste.what: Looked up the layers()/B helper signatures and the palette state format by reading build.mjs and vocab.mjs
waste.cost: about 3 file reads
waste.tool: a short per-helper reference (B.* states, large_fern half, leaves persistent) printed by the toolkit

waste.what: Ran the mcd CLI via a $MCD variable, which zsh did not word-split, so the first calls failed
waste.cost: one failed call
waste.tool: a wrapper bin on PATH (e.g. `mcd` shim) so the workers do not need the full node path in a variable

waste.what: Checked the room render and the house tiles by eye; the house check lists other parts' floating y=5 header blocks mixed with mine
waste.cost: two image reads

summary:
